extracted.intended_audience: patent prosecutors (attorneys/agents) arguing 35 U.S.C. §103 rejections before the USPTO and courts
extracted.subtask_description: Practical prosecution tactics for defeating obviousness rejections after KSR by attacking the specific KSR rationales and marshaling objective evidence. Focuses on which legal showings and factual proof (e.g., declarations, secondary considerations) are most effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attack each KSR rationale on its own terms
rubrics_metrics.description: KSR International v. Teleflex (2007) loosened the TSM test. Examiners now combine references using KSR rationales: "obvious to try," "design choice," "known technique applied to known problem," "predictable variations." Practitioners must learn to attack each rationale on its own terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize which KSR rationale the examiner is using and tailor rebuttal arguments to that rationale rather than relying on pre-KSR TSM-only thinking. Enumerate and rebut the specific rationale invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious to Try
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit has narrowed "obvious to try": the prior art must (a) identify a finite number of identified, predictable solutions, (b) suggest the inventor's chosen solution, and (c) provide a reasonable expectation of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the prior art did not present a finite/predictable set, did not single out the claimed solution, or did not create a reasonable expectation that the chosen option would work. Example: if prior art lists five candidates and the inventor chose the third, "obvious to try" should apply only if there was reasonable expectation that the third would work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hindsight Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner combinations often work only because the examiner knows the answer. Argue that without the inventor's disclosure, a POSITA would not have selected those specific references from the universe of available art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the distortion caused by hindsight and, where helpful, cite KSR's admonition: "A factfinder should be aware, of course, of the distortion caused by hindsight bias." Show why the asserted combination is not a natural or predictable selection absent the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching Away
rubrics_metrics.description: If a cited reference says "do not use approach X" or "X has been shown to fail," that reference teaches away from a combination using X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit teachings away to negate motivation to combine. Highlight language in references that discourages or reports failures of the claimed approach; teaching-away arguments directly undercut the examiner's asserted motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Reasonable Expectation of Success
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a POSITA would have been motivated to combine, an obviousness rejection requires reasonable expectation that the combination would work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press that expectation-of-success is missing, particularly in unpredictable arts (chemistry, biology). Argue unpredictability or technical uncertainties to show that routine experimentation would not have provided a reasonable expectation of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bodily Incorporation Required (incompatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes references cannot be combined without destroying the function of one. If reference A teaches a high-temperature process and reference B teaches a temperature-sensitive component, combining them is non-trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that the asserted combination requires more than what a POSITA would do absent inventive insight because the teachings are incompatible or would negate functionality. Use technical explanation to show that the combination is not a 'simple' or routine substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Considerations - Use Them
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial success, long-felt need, failure of others, copying by competitors, industry praise, unexpected results, licensing/acquiescence by others - these are objective indicators of non-obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie each secondary consideration to a nexus with the claimed features. Present evidence (sales data, testimony, press, licensing agreements) and submit it via 1.132 declarations or include it in the prosecution response itself to strengthen the non-obviousness case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations Beat Argument
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration from an expert in the field carries far more weight than attorney argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For close cases, invest in an expert declaration that explains why a POSITA would not have combined the references or would have lacked a reasonable expectation of success. Use 1.132 declarations where appropriate; factual, technical attestations by experts are more persuasive than counsel's rhetoric.
